title: Is Vinyl Plank Flooring Really Waterproof? Basements, Bathrooms and Leaks
meta: Vinyl plank is waterproof; the subfloor is not. Wills Flooring explains what LVP survives in Seattle basements, bathrooms and leaks, plus $2.50/sq ft labor.
keywords: is vinyl plank flooring waterproof, waterproof vinyl plank basement Seattle, LVP flooding what happens, vinyl plank bathroom waterproof, luxury vinyl plank water damage subfloor

blocks.lead: The plank is waterproof. The floor is not. Rigid-core vinyl plank will not swell, warp or stain from water sitting on it, but water still runs through the seams and the perimeter gap to whatever is underneath.
blocks.detail: That distinction decides everything about basements, bathrooms and leaks. In Seattle, where the questions usually involve a 1920s basement or a condo dishwasher, vinyl plank is still the best hard-surface answer, as long as you understand what it does and does not protect. Wills Flooring installs it for $2.50 per sq ft in labor.

blocks.html: A common Reddit thread goes: "Our washer hose let go, the LVP looks perfect, so we are fine, right?" Sometimes. The plank was fine; the plywood under it was soaked. The word waterproof on the box is true and also incomplete, and in a city as wet as Seattle that gap matters. Here is what the label means, where water actually goes, what we check before installing in a Ballard or Beacon Hill basement, and what happens after a real leak.

blocks.text: What waterproof means on the box

items.title: SPC and WPC vinyl plank
items.text: The core is stone-plastic or wood-plastic composite. Neither absorbs water, so a plank left in a bucket for a week comes out unchanged. This is what waterproof means: the material does not swell, delaminate or grow mold on its own. It says nothing about the joints between planks.

items.title: Flexible LVT
items.text: Thin, flexible vinyl tiles and planks glued to the subfloor. Also waterproof as a material, and because there is no air gap under them, less water reaches the subfloor. The trade-off is that a flooded glue-down floor usually has to be scrapped, because you cannot lift it to dry things out.

items.title: Water-resistant laminate
items.text: Laminate has a wood-fiber core. Newer lines seal the edges and survive a spill for a day; they do not survive a leak. If a box says water-resistant instead of waterproof, that is the difference between a wiped-up spill and a wet subfloor.

items.title: The warranty fine print
items.text: Every waterproof warranty we have read covers the plank and excludes the subfloor, standing water beyond 24 to 72 hours, flooding and leaks from appliances. It protects you from a defective plank, not from a burst hose. Plan your installation as if the warranty did not exist.

items.d: A spill or a wet dog
items.text: Stays on top. Wipe it up within a few hours and nothing happens. This is the everyday case and vinyl plank wins it outright.
items.note: Even a pet accident overnight is usually harmless if cleaned in the morning.

items.text: Seeps through the click joints and the expansion gap at the walls. Plywood or OSB under it starts to swell; concrete traps water between slab and plank.
items.note: A dishwasher that runs and leaks all cycle is enough.

items.text: Trapped moisture under a floating floor has nowhere to dry. That is when the musty smell starts and when the subfloor edges cup and lift plank joints.
items.note: The plank still looks fine, which is the trap.

items.text: Click-lock vinyl plank can be unclicked from the nearest wall, stacked, the subfloor dried with fans for a few days, and the same planks put back. A glue-down or a laminate cannot.
items.note: We have done this after several Seattle water-heater failures.

blocks.text: Bathrooms, kitchens and laundry rooms: the details that keep water out

items.html: Silicone the wet perimeter. Along the tub, the shower curb and around the toilet flange we fill the expansion gap with 100 percent silicone instead of leaving it open under the trim. That is the main entry point for bath water.
Put a pan under the washer. A washer supply line is the most common flood in Seattle condos and the one most likely to reach the unit below. A drain pan and braided hoses matter more than the floor.
Keep seams away from the dishwasher. We lay out planks so a full-width plank sits under the dishwasher and fridge rather than a joint. Fewer seams where leaks start.
Run the fan. Vinyl plank does not care about steam. Your drywall, cabinets and the subfloor edges do. A fan on a 20-minute timer protects everything the floor cannot.
Condo rules first. Many Capitol Hill and Queen Anne buildings require a sound-rated underlayment. We pick a pad that meets the HOA number and still has a vapor rating.

blocks.text: After a real leak: what to do with a vinyl plank floor

a.title: Usually salvageable
items: Lift planks from the nearest wall back to dry area
Dry the subfloor with fans and a dehumidifier for 3 to 5 days
Check plywood for swelling and mold; replace bad sheets
Reinstall the same planks; a few damaged locking edges may need replacing from your leftover box

b.title: Usually replaced
items: Glue-down planks tear when lifted and cannot be reused
Water trapped more than a week means the subfloor is the problem, not the floor
Concrete slabs need to dry back below the adhesive limit before anything goes down
Insurance adjusters often approve replacement once the subfloor is involved

blocks.title: Keep a box:
blocks.text: Always keep one unopened carton of your vinyl plank. Colors are discontinued every couple of years, and after a leak that spare box is the difference between a repair and a whole-room replacement.
Honest limits of waterproof vinyl plank

items.html: Heat is a bigger enemy than water. South-facing Seattle windows and radiant heat over 85°F make planks expand and buckle. Waterproof is not heatproof.
The subfloor still has to be flat and dry. A waterproof plank on a wet slab is a mold farm with a nice top. Moisture testing is not optional.
It is not a moisture barrier for your house. If a basement leaks, fix the leak. Covering it with vinyl plank hides the evidence until the smell arrives.

Some rooms still want tile. A curbless shower floor, a steam shower or a mudroom drain are tile jobs. Vinyl plank belongs everywhere else in the bathroom. See our vinyl plank installation page for what we include.

faq.q: Can water get under vinyl plank flooring?
faq.a: Yes. Click joints and the expansion gap along the walls let standing water through to the subfloor. The plank itself stays undamaged, which is why a floor can look perfect over a soaked subfloor. Wipe spills within hours, and after a real leak lift the planks and dry underneath.

faq.q: Is vinyl plank a good choice for a Seattle basement?
faq.a: It is the best hard-surface choice for most Seattle basements, provided the slab tests dry or is corrected first. Rigid-core planks handle the humidity swings of a 1920s basement without swelling. We test the concrete at the free estimate and add a vapor-rated underlayment when the numbers call for it.

faq.q: Does vinyl plank need to be sealed in a bathroom?
faq.a: The planks do not, but the perimeter does. We seal the expansion gap at the tub, shower and toilet with 100 percent silicone so bath water cannot run under the floor. Everywhere else the gap is left open under the baseboard so the floor can move.

faq.q: What happens to vinyl plank in a flood?
faq.a: The planks survive; the subfloor is the concern. A floating floor can be lifted, the subfloor dried for several days and the same planks reinstalled. Glue-down vinyl usually has to be replaced. Either way, water left under the floor for more than a few days leads to mold and odor.
